newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Investigation begins into Dutch Dakota crash.
newsitem.headline: Investigation begins into Dutch Dakota crash.

text.p: Dutch accident investigators on Thursday began the grim task of sifting through the wreckage of a crashed Dakota DC-3 aircraft, which plunged into the North Sea on Wednesday killing all 32 people on board.

"We have now recovered all 32 bodies. There were no survivors. I have heard identification (of the bodies) may take a number of days because of the injuries sustained," coastguard spokesman Gerrit Miedema told Reuters.

The World War Two vintage aircraft, carrying 26 passengers and six crew, was owned by the Dutch Dakota Association and was carrying a group of civil servants and club members on the return leg of a pleasure trip from Amsterdam to Texel, an island off the Dutch coast.
The cause of the crash is still unknown but, shortly before the plane ditched into the sea off the naval town of Den Helder, the pilot radioed that he had engine trouble.
"He had indicated that he wanted to make an emergency landing at the naval airbase De Kooy. He had a problem with one engine and somehow something went wrong," a navy spokesman said.
Crash investigators will be hampered by the absence of any flight recorder as they search for clues, ANP news agency said.
Anne Groeneveld, president of the DDA, said the aircraft was in perfect technical condition and had recently been checked by the national civil aviation authority.
Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands expressed deep shock over the crash, and was said by an official spokesman to have anxiously followed the disaster unfolding on Dutch television.
Prime Minister Wim Kok returned from an official visit to Luxembourg to comfort the relatives of the victims and crew who had gathered at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport.
